[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/opencr)](https://pypi.org/project/opencr/)

Collisional-radiative (CR) models of low-temperature plasmas in Python: explicit states and
reactions with traceable data, steady-state and time-dependent population kinetics, effective
ionization, recombination and emission coefficients, and synthetic spectra. Atomic hydrogen
first; molecular hydrogen, accelerated backends (cunumpy, JAX) and surrogate models are
optional extensions. Cross sections and rates come from
[plasmacoll](https://github.com/max-models/plasmacoll).

Documentation: <https://max-models.github.io/opencr/>

## Example

```python
import opencr

model = opencr.load_model("hydrogen/atomic/basic")
conditions = opencr.Conditions(
    electron_temperature=2.0,  # eV
    electron_density=1e18,  # m^-3
    densities={"H(n=1)": 1e19, "H+": 1e18},  # the drivers, m^-3
)
result = model.solve_steady_state(conditions)
result.populations["H(n=3)"]  # m^-3
result.emission().sel(line="A:3-2")  # H-alpha
result.reduction.effective_rate("H(n=1)", "H+")  # S_CR, m^3/s
```

The physics, the closures and the units are in
[The CR model](https://max-models.github.io/opencr/guides/model/); the acceptance criteria
of the atomic hydrogen model in
[Verification](https://max-models.github.io/opencr/guides/verification/).

## Install

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
make install    # uv sync --extra dev, plus the pre-commit hooks
uv run opencr list
```

Or create and activate a Python environment (3.10 or newer):

```bash
python -m venv env
source env/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip
```

Install the code and requirements with pip:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

The optional extras `cunumpy`, `jax` and `ml` add the accelerated backends and the
surrogate models; the `test`, `docs` and `dev` extras install the test runner, the documentation tooling and
the linters:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Development

Formatting and linting use [ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/), type checking
[pyright](https://microsoft.github.io/pyright/), run by [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/)
and in CI:

```bash
make lint     # ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright
make test     # pytest with coverage
```

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/); see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Build docs

The documentation in `docs/` is an Astro + Starlight site: hand-written pages, the notebooks
in `tutorials/` executed and published as pages, complete Python scripts in `examples/`
published with their plots, and the API reference generated from the
docstrings with [starlight-pydocs](https://ewels.github.io/starlight-pydocs/). It needs
Node 22 or newer.

```bash
make docs-install     # npm packages and the Python docs extra
make docs-notebooks   # execute tutorials/*.ipynb and convert them to pages
make docs-examples    # run examples/*.py and publish their plots
make docs-dev         # live preview at http://localhost:4321/opencr/
make docs-build       # the static site in docs/dist
```

## Build the README

`README.md` is rendered from `README.qmd` with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/):

```bash
make readme
```

## Releases

Before merging a release to `main`, update the version in `pyproject.toml`,
`src/opencr/__init__.py` and `CITATION.cff` (including its release date), and add the release
notes to `CHANGELOG.md`. The push to `main` creates a GitHub release with a `vX.Y.Z` tag and
publishes the package to PyPI with trusted publishing (OIDC). The one-time PyPI and GitHub
configuration is described in the
[publishing tutorial](https://max-models.github.io/opencr/development/publishing/).
